children: Shares of Bajaj Finance hit an intraday high of Rs 1,041, rising more than 3%, on September 23 as the stock snapped its two-session fall after investment bank UBS upgraded its recommendation to "neutral" from "sell".
The stock was the top Nifty gainer on September 23. Its target price was also raised to Rs 1,100 from Rs 910.

India's non-bank lenders could be entering a fresh unsecured credit growth cycle, led by a recovery in personal loans, said UBS. The investment banker expects healthy asset quality, abundant system liquidity, and a more risk-on stance among lenders to support growth. UBS sees personal loan growth to be around 30% for non-banking financial companies and 9% for banks and expects this recovery to benefit private banks and large NBFCs with established personal-loan franchises.

"With gold prices stabilising and, thus, likely gold loan growth moderation, a key substitute for personal loans over past few years could lose some momentum. This may benefit private banks and large NBFCs with strong personal loan franchises," said UBS.
Regarding Bajaj Finance, UBS said: "Expect cyclical EPS upgrades on yield-accretive growth and strong asset quality, though its valuation remains demanding."
At 1:05 pm on September 23, Bajaj Finance shares were trading 2.5% higher at Rs 1,034.2 apiece.

Global brokerage Jefferies sees a strong outlook for Bajaj Finance. In the near-term, the company is expected to see strong demand, asset quality, and efficiencies, leading to a tad lower net interest margin. Over the next 10 years, the company's management plans to grow assets under management at a compound annual growth rate of 23%.
Jefferies maintained a Buy rating with a target of Rs 1,280.

title: Bajaj Finance shares rise 3% as UBS upgrades to 'neutral', raises target price
